description: We are a multidisciplinary team combining astronomy, AI, software engineering, and game design. Our team includes an astrophysics PhD researcher, a senior software engineer experienced in LLMs and backend development, an AI engineer specializing in ML, RAG, Agentic AI and HCI, and a game designer.
summary:
Earthsignal is an interactive, scroll-driven story that makes land subsidence visible with real NISAR radar data. We turned 36 NISAR radar pairs into a time-lapse showing parts of Tehran sinking about 30 cm a year, which visitors explore one satellite pass at a time. 

Hands-on models of an aquifer, a 3D city and a radar echo explain why the ground sinks and how satellites measure it. An optional five-mission game, guided by Echo, turns these lessons into playable investigations where visitors experiment, interpret evidence and explore possible responses.

For deeper research, an advanced workspace supports satellite-data discovery, radar-image comparisons, point and area analysis, spatial profiles, and downloadable results with sources and uncertainty attached.

Earthsignal answers *Dancing with the SARs* by connecting accessible storytelling and play with scientific exploration. That matters because subsidence can quietly damage homes, roads and pipes before its effects become obvious.
details:
How it works: Earthsignal is a scroll-driven story about Tehran’s sinking ground. Hands-on scenes explain the cause: draining an aquifer, a 3D city under strain, and a radar echo from orbit. A time-lapse built from 36 real NISAR radar pairs then shows four months of ground motion. Click any spot to see how far it sank, up to about 30 cm a year.

Benefits: it makes slow, invisible damage easy for anyone to see, uses real data that’s honest about its limits, and shows through Tokyo’s example that subsidence can be slowed.

Impact: it makes invisible, slow damage easy to see and understand, while staying honest about uncertainty. We want people to notice subsidence early, while it can still be slowed.

Creativity: hands-on models (an aquifer, a 3D city, a radar echo), a five-mission game with a narrated guide, and research tools for exploring NISAR and Canadian Space Agency RADARSAT data pixel by pixel.

Tools: TypeScript, React, three.js and Leaflet for the web app. Python with GDAL and h5py for processing; NASA Earthdata and OpenStreetMap for data; hosted on an Ubuntu server.

Factors we considered: scientific accuracy, accessibility, mobile performance, open data, and simplicity for newcomers with depth for experts.
